section_title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
text: A consumer complaint relating to goods sold or delivered, or services provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with the District Consumer Commission by the consumer and certain other permitted complainants. The complaint may be filed electronically in the prescribed manner and is subject to the applicable fee and procedure.
pathway: Consumer grievance/dispute process may be relevant; verify the current forum and procedure.
authority: District Consumer Commission / Department of Consumer Affairs; verify current jurisdiction and filing route.

text: The Consumer Protection Act establishes District, State and National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions and sets out their jurisdiction and procedures. Current pecuniary jurisdiction should be verified against the applicable Act and rules before advising a user where to file.
pathway: Identify the appropriate Consumer Commission after checking the current pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction.
authority: District/State/National Consumer Commission as applicable; Department of Consumer Affairs.
verification_status: Official Act structure checked; current jurisdiction should be verified before use

text: The Consumer Protection Act provides for reference of appropriate consumer disputes to mediation in accordance with the Act and applicable procedure.
pathway: Where legally suitable, check whether consumer mediation is available before or during the complaint process.
authority: Consumer Commission / applicable consumer mediation mechanism.

text: Section 66C addresses fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's electronic signature, password or other unique identification feature.
pathway: Preserve digital evidence and consider the appropriate cyber-crime/police reporting route based on the facts.
authority: Police / cyber-crime reporting mechanism; verify the current reporting route.

act: Information Technology Act, 2000; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
section_title: Cheating by personation using computer resource; cheating
text: Section 66D of the Information Technology Act addresses cheating by personation using a computer resource or communication device. Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita addresses cheating. The exact offence and applicable provision depend on the facts.
pathway: Preserve transaction and communication evidence and use the appropriate cyber-crime/police reporting channel.
authority: Cyber-crime reporting mechanism / Police; verify the applicable process.

topic: Privacy / obscene or sexually explicit electronic material
section_title: Violation of privacy and electronic obscene/sexually explicit material
text: The Information Technology Act contains provisions addressing violation of privacy and publication or transmission of obscene or sexually explicit material in electronic form. Applicability depends on the facts and content involved.
pathway: Preserve the original digital evidence, avoid further distribution, and consider the cyber-crime/police reporting route.
authority: Cyber-crime reporting mechanism / Police.

act: Code on Wages, 2019; Industrial Relations Code, 2020
section: Section 17, Code on Wages; Section 59, Industrial Relations Code
section_title: Time limit for payment of wages; recovery of money due from employer
text: The Code on Wages contains provisions on the time limit for payment of wages. Section 59 of the Industrial Relations Code provides a recovery mechanism for money due to a worker in the circumstances specified by that Code, including an application to the appropriate Government subject to its conditions.
pathway: Labour/employment grievance pathway; identify the competent authority and applicable provision for the worker's facts.
authority: Competent labour authority / tribunal as applicable; DLSA/TLSC may assist eligible persons.

text: The Code on Wages contains provisions concerning payment of minimum wages, overtime wages and permitted deductions from wages. The exact entitlement depends on the employee, establishment and applicable rules.
pathway: Check the applicable labour provisions and competent authority before making a claim.
authority: Competent labour authority; verify applicable jurisdiction and procedure.

text: The Industrial Relations Code provides mechanisms for investigation and settlement of industrial disputes and includes Section 59 on recovery of money due from an employer. The appropriate route depends on the nature of the employment dispute and applicable provisions.
pathway: Use the applicable labour dispute-resolution mechanism after checking the facts and jurisdiction.
authority: Competent labour authority / tribunal as applicable.

text: The Hindu Marriage Act provides grounds and procedures for matrimonial proceedings and specifies the court to which petitions are to be presented. Applicability depends on the parties and the facts.
pathway: A matrimonial/family-court pathway may be relevant; verify personal-law applicability and jurisdiction.
authority: Competent Family Court/Court as applicable; legal-aid services may assist eligible persons.

section_title: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings
text: Where the statutory conditions are met, the court may order payment of expenses of proceedings and monthly support during a proceeding under the Act when a spouse lacks sufficient independent income for support and necessary expenses.
pathway: Consider the appropriate matrimonial/family proceeding and check eligibility with the competent court or legal-aid provider.
authority: Competent court / Family Court as applicable.

text: In proceedings under the Act, the court may make orders concerning custody, maintenance and education of minor children in accordance with the statutory provision and the circumstances of the case.
pathway: Family-court/court pathway may be relevant; the court considers the circumstances of the child and case.
authority: Competent Family Court/Court.

text: Section 6 provides a route for a person seeking information under the RTI Act to make a request in writing or electronically to the appropriate Public Information Officer or through the prescribed assistant officer, subject to the Act's requirements.
pathway: If the grievance is about obtaining information held by a public authority, an RTI request may be relevant.
authority: Central or State Public Information Officer, as applicable.

text: Section 7 sets out the statutory framework for disposal of an RTI request, including communication of the decision and applicable information/fee provisions.
pathway: For an RTI request that has not been properly processed, check the statutory RTI appeal/grievance route.
authority: Public Information Officer and, where applicable, the designated appellate/Information Commission route.

section: Not a single universal statutory section
text: The dataset identifies many government-service problems as administrative grievances that may be resolved through the concerned department's grievance mechanism or other applicable official channel. The correct route depends on the service, department and jurisdiction.
pathway: First identify the concerned department/service and use its official grievance mechanism; use broader public-grievance channels where applicable.
authority: Concerned government department/grievance mechanism; CPGRAMS may apply to covered central-government grievances.
verification_status: Dataset-derived administrative guidance; service-specific rules must be checked

text: Section 12 identifies categories of persons who are entitled to legal services when the statutory criteria are met, including specified vulnerable or disadvantaged groups and other persons covered by the provision.
pathway: Check eligibility and apply through the appropriate Legal Services Institution.
authority: DLSA / TLSC / KSLSA / NALSA, depending on the matter and jurisdiction.

text: Section 13 addresses entitlement to legal services for persons satisfying the Section 12 criteria, subject to the statutory conditions concerning the person's case and the concerned Legal Services Authority.
pathway: Submit the legal-aid request to the appropriate Legal Services Institution and follow its verification/application process.
authority: DLSA / TLSC / KSLSA / NALSA.

section_title: Organisation and award of Lok Adalats
text: The Legal Services Authorities Act provides for organisation of Lok Adalats and their handling of appropriate disputes for amicable settlement, subject to the statutory framework.
pathway: Check whether the dispute is suitable for Lok Adalat and contact the relevant Legal Services Institution.
authority: DLSA / TLSC / KSLSA / NALSA.

section_title: Claims Tribunals and application for compensation
text: The Motor Vehicles Act provides for Claims Tribunals and an application route for compensation arising from motor vehicle accidents, subject to the Act and applicable procedure.
pathway: For an accident compensation claim, check the applicable MACT/insurer/police route based on the facts.
authority: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) / insurer / police as applicable.

section_title: Special provisions as to compensation in case of hit and run motor accident
text: Section 161 contains special provisions concerning compensation in specified hit-and-run motor accidents, subject to the statutory conditions and applicable scheme/procedure.
pathway: For a hit-and-run matter, preserve accident evidence and check the statutory compensation route and applicable official scheme.
authority: Applicable government/claims mechanism, police and other authorities as prescribed.

section_title: Award and procedure of Claims Tribunal
text: The Motor Vehicles Act provides for the award of the Claims Tribunal and the procedure and powers of the Tribunal in motor accident compensation matters.
pathway: Check the MACT procedure and applicable filing requirements for the specific accident claim.
authority: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

section_title: Filing of complaints with the Authority or adjudicating officer
text: Section 31 provides a route for an aggrieved person to file a complaint with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority or the adjudicating officer, as applicable under the Act.
pathway: For a covered real-estate dispute involving a promoter/project, check the applicable RERA authority and complaint route.
authority: State/UT Real Estate Regulatory Authority or adjudicating officer, as applicable.

text: The dataset identifies land ownership, boundary, encroachment, inheritance and possession disputes as property matters. The appropriate forum depends on whether the issue concerns title, possession, land records, government land or a regulated real-estate project.
pathway: First identify whether the dispute concerns civil title/possession, revenue records, government land or RERA; then approach the competent authority/court.
authority: Competent Civil Court / revenue authority / RERA authority depending on the dispute.
source_type: Official statutory source plus dataset-derived routing
verification_status: Routing is dataset-derived; issue-specific law must be verified

text: The dataset includes disputes involving security deposits, rent receipts, landlord entry, non-payment of rent and refusal to vacate. The applicable law and forum depend on the state, tenancy arrangement and facts.
pathway: Check the applicable state tenancy/rent law and the competent forum before taking action.
authority: Competent rent/civil authority or court depending on the state and dispute.
source_type: Official statutory repository; state-specific law must be verified
verification_status: Dataset-derived routing; state-specific law must be verified

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
text: An aggrieved person, a Protection Officer or another person on her behalf may present an application to the Magistrate seeking relief under the Act. The Act provides for consideration of a Domestic Incident Report where applicable.
pathway: Safety-first response; consider the Magistrate/Protection Officer route and immediate police assistance where there is danger.
authority: Magistrate / Protection Officer / Police as applicable; DLSA/TLSC may assist eligible persons.

act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
section_title: Protection, residence, monetary relief and custody orders
text: The Act provides for protection orders and, subject to its conditions, residence orders, monetary relief and temporary custody orders in domestic-violence proceedings.
pathway: Seek appropriate protection and other relief through the statutory process; use emergency police assistance where immediate safety is at risk.
authority: Magistrate / Protection Officer / Police as applicable.

act: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
text: The dataset identifies workplace sexual harassment as a high-risk category where an internal complaints mechanism and, depending on the facts, police/legal-aid pathways may be relevant. The applicable complaint mechanism depends on the workplace and statutory conditions.
pathway: Preserve evidence and consider the workplace complaints mechanism and appropriate legal/police route based on the facts.
authority: Internal Committee/competent workplace mechanism; Police or other authority where applicable; DLSA/TLSC may assist eligible persons.
source_type: Official statutory repository; exact POSH provision should be verified from the current Act text
verification_status: Dataset-derived routing; exact provision must be verified

act: UGC (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023
text: The UGC lists the University Grants Commission (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023 as the current student-grievance regulation. The appropriate institutional grievance mechanism and escalation route depend on the institution and grievance.
pathway: Use the institution's designated student-grievance mechanism and the applicable UGC framework; escalate according to the prescribed process where necessary.
authority: Institutional grievance mechanism / university authority / applicable UGC framework.

act: UGC (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023; applicable education regulations
text: The dataset includes fee disputes, withholding of certificates and other student grievances. The applicable rule and authority depend on whether the institution is a university, college, school or another education provider and on the nature of the complaint.
pathway: First use the institution's grievance mechanism and identify the applicable university/education authority before escalating.
authority: Institutional grievance mechanism / university or education authority as applicable.
source_type: Official UGC source plus dataset-derived routing
verification_status: Dataset-derived routing; applicable education rules must be verified

act: Applicable anti-ragging framework and UGC regulations
text: Student-safety complaints such as ragging or serious harassment require the applicable institutional and statutory reporting route. The exact authority depends on the incident and institution.
pathway: Prioritize immediate safety, preserve evidence and report through the institution and appropriate authorities as required.
authority: Institutional authorities / Police / applicable education authority.
verification_status: Dataset-compatible routing; incident-specific law must be verified
